result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as a mock-resources folder, whatever follows in the name. I haven't added tests for the new cases. The only run was the existing tests matching `*Convention*`, which passed. I didn't run the full module tests.

In `ScopingConventions.java` (around line 393), I changed the two "Mock resources" conventions from `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` to `.*/__mock[^/\\]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/\\]*/.*`.

- **Newly covered:** a plain `mock/` folder, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/` and `mock模拟/`. The old rule required at least one ASCII letter, digit, `_`, `-` or space after `mock`. The new one allows any characters except a path separator.
- **Single folder name:** the name after `mock` can't contain `/` or `\`, so the match stays inside one folder. `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` don't match.
- **Backslash paths:** `SourceFileFilter.matches` already tries each path with `\` converted to `/`, so Windows-style paths work with the same pattern.
- **Still matched:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` all match the new pattern.
- **Leading slash:** like the old rule, the pattern needs a `/` before `mock`, so a path that starts directly with `mock/` and has no leading slash still isn't matched.
